topic: Unchunked Prefill Cripples Local LLM Latency
postText:
You spin up an open-weight 70B model on an on-prem dual-A100 server for a busy hospital floor. Everything runs blisteringly fast until an ICU doctor dumps a dense, 8,000-token multi-day clinical chart for immediate summarization. Instantly, active generation for three nurses typing discharge orders freezes mid-sentence.

Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) skyrockets from 45ms to 8,500ms. In local deployments, naive inference runtimes treat prompt prefill and token decoding as monolithic sequential steps. Compute-heavy matrix multiplications for massive prompt ingestion monopolize tensor cores, effectively starving memory-bandwidth-bound decode steps waiting for their next single token.

To keep local hospital LLMs production-ready, apply three hardware-aligned patterns:
1. Chunked Prefill: Split mammoth context windows into uniform chunks (e.g., 512 tokens), interleaving prefill slices with running decode steps to bound scheduling delay.
2. Continuous Batching: Evict requests at the iteration level instead of locking fixed batch slots until all generations finish.
3. Paged Memory Pools: Decouple virtual key-value blocks from physical VRAM to banish internal memory fragmentation and drop OOM failures to zero.

Predictable decode latency always beats raw prompt ingestion throughput in mission-critical edge deployments.
